focus: A15 verification design: a two-version doctor and CI check. Specify concrete, scriptable checks that prove the repo works on whichever version is installed, using only facts this run has proven. Known checks: - v2 plugin status: `opencode2 api GET "/api/plugin?location%5Bdirectory%5D=<enc>"`, raw query, output redirected to a file because piped output truncates, retried because the first call returns before discovery. Each repo plugin should show `state.status == "active"`. - v2 agent, command and skill registration: `opencode2 debug agents`, `/api/command` and `/api/skill`, raw query. - v1: `opencode debug config </dev/null` loads plugins without a model call, and `opencode debug agent <name>` and `opencode debug skill` exist. Each version calls only its own entry. - A model-free smoke test that loads plugins and passes env, on both versions: `run --standalone -m nosuchprovider/nosuchmodel` on v2. Find the v1 equivalent. Investigate how v1 can report per-plugin load success or failure without a status API, for example logs under `opencode debug paths` or a marker convention. Find where the repo's existing doctor framework lives (`/doctor:*` command docs under `.skilled/commands/doctor/` and their scripts) and where a new `/doctor:opencode` or similar check would slot in. Design a CI job that installs both versions side by side in separate npm prefixes. Output: a check list (command, expected output, pass rule) for v1, v2 and both, the doctor integration point with file paths, and the CI job outline. Do not install anything. Never run `opencode2 service stop`, `start` or `restart`, or `uninstall`. Never edit repo files outside this packet.

label: v1 has a model-free discovery oracle: `opencode debug config </dev/null` exits 0 and prints top-level `plugin` (file:// spec array) plus `plugin_origins` ({spec,source,scope}) covering all 16 repo plugins, with no server, no model call and zero plugin evaluation (0 fresh log lines across a 742,350-byte resolution).

v1 has no per-plugin status API but has a per-plugin outcome log: INFO msg="loading plugin" id=<abs> entrypoint=file://<abs> for each plugin that loaded, and WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=<abs> ref=err_<hex> cause="Cause([Fail(PluginModule.LoadError: ..." for each that did not. Both shapes were observed against this repo's own 16 plugin paths, so a doctor leg can decide per file from the log window under `opencode debug paths` -> log, with no custom marker convention.

`opencode debug config` resolves discovery but does not load modules. A full successful resolution produced zero new log lines, so discovery and load outcome must be two separate doctor legs: inventory from debug config, load success from the log during an actual load.

The repo's own guard denies a nested `opencode run` issued from a Pi agent: "Pi dispatch denied for cli-opencode. Name the matching executor in the user request." A /doctor:opencode leg therefore cannot shell out to `opencode run` when the doctor runs inside Pi; the load leg must use debug config plus log reading or report SKIP/DEGRADED, and belongs in CI where no Pi guard is present.

v1 discovery is a union, not an override: one resolution of plugin_origins contains a scope=global user plugin together with project-scoped plugins, so an ancestor-level install stays visible from a deeper cwd.

v1 normalises the config key to `plugin` (singular) in resolved output regardless of authored spelling: the resolved top-level key set is [plugin, plugin_origins]. Any check asserting config shape must assert the resolved form, and this does not settle whether v1 accepts `plugins` (plural) on input.
A15 verification design: doctor and CI checks for v1 and v2
v1 debug config exposes plugin and plugin_origins
v1 log carries loading plugin and failed to load plugin lines
repo guard denies nested opencode run from Pi

direction: `opencode debug config` as a v1 plugin-load smoke test
reason: It resolves plugin inventory but instantiates nothing: zero log lines for 16 discovered plugins. It is a discovery check only.
